title: A published signal-clustering CAN masquerade detector did not reproduce from its description, and capture length looks like a confound
problem: Masquerade attacks on a vehicle CAN bus keep normal message timing, so timing-based detectors miss them; ORNL published a correlation-structure detector aimed at exactly that gap, but its code is closed.
mechanism: [KNOWN: OSTI 1866690] Each whole capture is translated to signal time series, resampled to 10 Hz, turned into a Pearson correlation matrix and clustered hierarchically (single, complete, average, Ward). Dendrograms are compared with CluSim element-centric similarity (alpha 0.9, r -5.0), and a Mann-Whitney test asks whether attack-vs-benign similarities fall below benign-vs-benign similarities. The paper reports Ward significance for all five ROAD masquerade categories and F1 of about 90-94% over 220 folds.
finding: [KNOWN: recorded experiment, 2026-11-15] An independent rebuild (not ORNL's code) on ROAD's released signal files, with predictions hashed before any data was extracted, found Ward significant in 0 of 5 categories (smallest two-sided p 0.199) and flagged 1 of 13 masquerade captures. The global constant filter removed every injected field because some captures hold those fields constant. The only variant with significance (per-pair signal sets, 3 of 5) ran in the wrong direction, attack captures looking more similar to benign ones, and stayed significant with the target ID's signals removed. Clean pre-injection segments were significant in 3 of 5 categories and length-matched benign crops in 25% of category tests, so capture length and driving regime drive the test more than the injection does. [INFERRED] The closed code may make choices the paper does not state, or use a different signal translation; a non-reproduction does not show the original results are wrong.

experiment.revision: independent rebuild from OSTI 1866690 (PDF md5 27f8aa0e05691288e8f67734c151b31a); no ORNL code
experiment.command: sh atlas/labs/can-signal-clustering-rebuild/run.sh env dups prep r0 r0check sens a3 q1 diag q2g q3g q2p q2pi q2pc0 q2pc1 q3p
experiment.limitations: Independent rebuild of a closed implementation from its paper; ten ambiguities were resolved by stated choices and only one variant was changed at a time. Python 3.10.20 with clusim 0.4, python-igraph 0.9.9, scipy 1.9.3, numpy 1.23.5 and pandas 1.5.3 on macOS arm64. Requires the ROAD dataset (not committed). Mann-Whitney on pairwise similarities treats dependent values as independent. Offline replay of one vehicle's dynamometer captures. The deviation dates in the README are self-attested; the predictions file hash is not.

adaptation: [INFERRED] When judging a whole-capture CAN detector, add two controls before trusting a significant result: clean segments of the attack captures with the injection cut out, and benign crops matched to the attack captures' lengths. Report which signals survive preprocessing filters, since a filter can silently drop the attacked field.
unknowns: Whether any coherent set of preprocessing choices, such as a union signal set with constant signals kept or a fresh DBC translation of the raw logs, reproduces the paper's Ward column in the right direction.
What the closed DOE CODE 134139 implementation actually does differently, and what its probability score means.
Whether ORNL's later public windowed code (DOE CODE 141444) avoids the length confound.
